key_insight: Multiscale simulations identify a dynamically stabilized hexagonal ZrO interlayer that shapes columnar oxide growth and acts as an oxygen diffusion barrier during zirconium corrosion.
engineering_relevance: Modeling oxide microstructure, transport barriers, and local tensile stresses could help assess zirconium corrosion kinetics and crack susceptibility.
method: Compute ZrOₓ properties using first-principles density functional theory.
Use a DFT-trained machine-learned potential for molecular dynamics simulations.
Inform phase-field simulations with thermochemistry, anisotropic elasticity, interfacial energies, diffusion, and heterogeneous grain nucleation.
evidence_signal: Simulations reproduce columnar oxide morphology and grain size distributions observed in micrographs, along with an undulatory metal/oxide interface.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative validation metrics and identifies the ZrO layer’s contribution to sub-parabolic corrosion kinetics as potential rather than established.
paper_title: Multiscale Modeling of Zr Corrosion: Predicting Microstructures of Oxide Films
